Generic company-wide programs, customer contracts and portfolio filings cannot be allocated to this project; negative portal results are coverage findings, not zero claims.

project_updates.title: Investment, construction, supplier and operating-model decisions — every candidate rejected
project_updates.notes: Investment candidate: converting 'multimillion-dollar,' the 2011 $2.697 million property purchase, 2014/2015 sale-leaseback prices or the $575 million portfolio sale into facility capital investment is rejected because the first is unbounded, deed prices are asset transfers and the portfolio price has no site allocation. Construction candidate: the rejected $5,000 right-of-way application cannot be summed or multiplied, and the opening-era retrofit lacks issued-permit value, audited outlay, asset mix, duration, workers, hours, payroll and local residence. Supplier/indirect candidate: applying an input-output multiplier or transferred local-purchase share is rejected because no eligible direct-spend base, paid vendor amount, multiplier vintage/geography or channel separation exists. Operations candidate: the 2012 release says the onsite NOC was staffed 24/7/365 and current specifications promise 24x7x365 onsite support/security. If these words proved one continuously occupied local post, the zero-leave arithmetic floor would be 8,760 coverage hours / (40 hours x 52 weeks) = 4.2115 FTE; a practical relief factor would increase it for leave, training, breaks and overlap. The model is rejected because the sources do not establish one dedicated occupied post, distinguish shared security/NOC/remote-hands functions, show whether coverage is local employees or contractors, or provide scheduled hours, relief factor, headcount, occupation mix, payroll or residence. A current vacancy and advertised wage band cannot fill those inputs. Leaving the operations/household metrics as gaps is more accurate than publishing a false staffing minimum.

project_updates.title: Fiscal, public-cost, resource and community-model decisions — no same-scope base survives
project_updates.notes: Fiscal candidate: signed Pulaski tables were opened for 2011-2025 and state millage reports for 2023-2025. Code 03/33 resolves the parcel to Little Rock city / Pulaski County Special School District. School/city/county/overall components are 40.7/15.6/8.5/64.8 mills in 2011, 40.7/15.2/8.5/64.4 in 2012, 40.7/15.1/8.5/64.3 in 2017-2020, 40.7/15.6/8.5/64.8 in 2021, and 40.7/15.1/8.5/64.3 in 2022-2026. Applying each rate to the canonical taxable values would yield modeled real-property bills of $31,912.70 (2011), $28,358.54 (2012), $31,146.28 (2017), $33,978.05 (2018), $36,809.82 (2019), $39,641.59 (2020), $42,803.64 (2021), $46,721.02 (2022), $50,968.68 (2023), $96,643.03 (2024) and $89,797.97 (2026). The last exactly matches the Assessor's current estimate, but the observed 2025 $82,440.85 Amount Due implies a $1,282,128.30 rate base at 64.3 mills, a base not present in the retained valuation history; applying 2024's $1,503,002 taxable value would overstate that charge by $14,202.18 (17.23%). Because 2025 valuation revisions are unresolved, receipts/payment status and personal-property accounts are missing, and the recipient table allocates a levy rather than cash receipts, the apparently mechanical series fails the requested 2025 calibration and is not published as contribution or distribution. A public-service-cost break-even identity is also rejected because an unpaid charge is not verified same-recipient revenue. Incentive counterfactuals remain unallocated; community annualization lacks a recipient amount. No synthesis fragment is added.

project_updates.title: GDP, employment and wage outcome decisions — 2012 is not a clean county treatment
project_updates.notes: The governed BEA/BLS county panel for Pulaski County FIPS 05119 was reviewed over 2001-2024 with candidate pre-periods ending in 2011, a 2012 opening anchor and possible post-periods through 2024. GDP candidate: difference-in-differences, event-study and synthetic-control approaches are rejected because the selected building was already a 1993 computer center, Acxiom had another Little Rock data center by fiscal 2006, the treatment intensity is unknown and concurrent headquarters/sector shocks cannot be separated. Employment candidate: the same timing and donor failures apply, and neither the current vacancy nor corporate headcounts measure facility or county job contribution. Wage candidate: the same identification failures apply; no facility payroll or occupation mix exists and county nominal average weekly wages mix inflation and industry composition. A descriptive county gap is also rejected as insufficiently decision-relevant because it cannot distinguish this small retrofit/operation from the diverse county economy. No county comparison is presented as a project effect and no public-records requests or other solicitations were made.
